identity.real_world_identity_notes: Brazilian sports car built between 1970 and 1980 on Volkswagen running gear, with a fibreglass body, an air-cooled flat four and a four-speed manual gearbox. Despite the GTE name it is a classic road-derived car rather than a GTE-class racer, and AMS2 classes it under Copa Classic B. Its controls match that: an H-pattern shift, the clutch needed to pull away, and no automation at all.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
This is a classic road-derived car rather than a GTE racer: H-pattern shift, clutch required to move off, and no automatic cut or blip.

Upshift throttle lift and downshift manual blip are set from the guided-drive method notes, which record that the upshift was accepted after a throttle lift and the downshift after the driver's own blip.

The category the simulator races this car in does not preserve its original gearbox. Copa Classic article 8.1 requires a casing from the car or engine maker but allows it to be freely reworked and makes the gears themselves free, and category B permits a more modern gearbox matched to the engine. So even naming the road car's Volkswagen transaxle would not establish what the raced car turns, and no reviewed source names it in any case.

Knowingly blocked on the downshift blip, recorded rather than carried quietly. The blip is `required` in authentic_controls on the strength of the guided drive, and a drive establishes what AMS2 demands rather than what the real car needed. Where the construction was later established for a car in this position - Formula Vee Gen2, Formula Vee FIN and the Diablo SV-R - the authentic value was revised to optional every time and the simulator's demand moved to an override. Three out of three. So this value is carried without corroboration and is more likely wrong than right; it stays because no source establishes the construction that would settle it, and the dataset does not convert a value by assumption.

What would unblock it: a competitor specification for the car as raced. Naming the road car's transaxle would not do it, because Copa Classic frees the gears and permits the casing to be reworked, so the category does not preserve the road car's internals.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.puma-gte.20260813t200837646z-e450e3e2 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the four-speed manual gearbox on Volkswagen running gear is supported by a registered secondary source.

claims.basis: A registered secondary source establishes the Puma GTE identity, its Volkswagen mechanicals and its four-speed manual gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The source specifies a four-speed manual gearbox, and the live drive confirmed four gears through an H-pattern shift. Whether that gearbox is synchromesh or dog engaged is not established and stays unknown.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
The guided drive recorded that a clutchless upshift was accepted after a throttle lift and a clutchless downshift after the driver's manual throttle blip, with no automatic cut or blip detected.

archetype.basis: No registered archetype is a four-speed H-pattern that needs the blip. The registered four-speed leaves it optional, and this car requires it. Whether that is a departure or a different mechanism turns on gearbox_type, which is unestablished: dog rings need the driver to match revs, which would make these cars an archetype of their own rather than a variation on the synchromesh one. Six curated cars sit in exactly this position. A reviewed source settles all of them together. This record also leaves the gate itself unrecorded.
